about: Published security advisories for the JavaScript libraries Gaugeline can recognise in a served file, read by library-with-advisory. Each advisory names the versions it affects (introduced is the first affected version, fixed the first version that is not; fixed is null when no fixed version is listed) and the page that publishes it. The entries were written from the public advisories as remembered and have not been compared with their pages: confirm each one before relying on it, then set verified to true and lastChecked to the day. Only advisories known to exist are listed; a library or version missing here is not a statement that it is safe.

packagesAbout: Published security advisories for npm packages, read by the checks that look at the version a repository installs (zod-version-advisory, next-version-advisory). The version comes from the lockfile, never from running anything. Each advisory lists the versions it affects in `affects` (introduced is the first affected version, fixed the first version that is not), and in `unconfirmed` the versions the advisory's published range reaches but that Gaugeline has not confirmed, or that have no fixed release: a version there is reported as not sure, never as a finding. A finding needs verified to be true. These entries were compared with the advisory's own page and with the npm registry's advisory answer for specific versions on the day in lastChecked; an advisory published after that day is not in the list, so a version that matches nothing here is not a statement that it is safe.
